notes.1: Option A was the most common incorrect answer. Candidates must take care to read the whole question. The indicator was to turn red, which required an acidic gas.
notes.7: Some candidates chose option B , incorrectly assuming that Group I and Group VII elements form covalent bonds.
notes.9: The question was one of the most demanding question on the paper. Options A and B were both popular answers.
notes.10: The question required candidates to recall the electrode product of two different electrolysis experiments. Some candidates chose one of the options, especially option D , which showed recall only of aqueous electrolysis.
notes.13: This was one of the more demanding questions on the paper. Candidates were required to recall how conditions change both reaction rate and the quantity of product produced. Option A was a common error.
notes.19: This question required candidates to use data on an unfamiliar compound to make a deduction about precipitation. All options were chosen equally, which suggested guessing.
notes.21: Fewer than half of the candidates were able to recall the role of the hydrogen ion in acidic solutions. Option D was the most common incorrect answer.
notes.23: Few candidates were distracted by option A or C . Option B was the most common incorrect answer, suggesting that the trend in density of Group I elements is not well known.
notes.30: Some candidates incorrectly chose option C .
notes.34: Some candidates were more likely to choose option C , which is a correct statement but does not answer the question.
notes.39: Candidates who performed less well were more likely to choose option C , where neither column of the table is correct.
notes.general_comments: Candidates found Questions 2 , 12 , 14 and 32 to have the least demand. Candidates found Questions 9 and 13 the most demanding. Candidates must take particular care when answering questions which contain a negative statement, such as ‘not’ or ‘cannot’. These were found in Questions 30 and 34 .
